quote: Human capacities are strengthened by the use of machines.
note: machines are God's creation; man's role is to control them

quote: No wonder, then, that the factory workers are deteriorating physically and mentally.
note: unhealthy, monotonous factory conditions degrade workers

quote: The man who relies on machines is not weak, but strong.
note: reliance draws on others' minds and bodies

quote: It does, because machines can do work that men can do, and thereby does away with the necessity for muscular effort, and hence renders the muscles less capable of effort.
There is no doubt that relying on machines weakens the human faculties.
note: blind reliance is a kind of superstition

quote: The result is that people are not as healthy as they ought to be.
Machines do not weaken human capacities; rather, they multiply them.
There is no doubt that the use of machinery, properly handled, is compatible with full human development for the worker.
note: skill in using machines grows; output rises without overstrain

quote: In the second place, using machines tends to weaken human capacities.
note: machines used only where capacities already weak (circular)

quote: Relying on machines does not weaken human capacities.
The wrong answer is that the use of machines weakens human capacities. It does not.
note: reliance is a good habit if not excessive

quote: The less he works with his hands, the more they are weakened.
To trust to a machine is a practice which, if kept up, tends to weaken the human capacities.
The mastery of the machine also is an admirable training in observation and accuracy, and the human touch is not altogether eliminated by the machine.
note: mastering machines trains learning, observation, accuracy

quote: It is quite natural that the machine should weaken the capacities of man, because it frees him from the necessity of using his capacity.
The legs are better off for having the crutches to lean on, and the brain is better off for having the machine to help it.
The machine does not weaken the man who uses it, but it weakens immensely the race of men that does not use it.
The human understanding and the human memory are not weakened by the use of machines, but it is only the memory of things which have been previously learned that is weakened.

We are all agreed that in the past the human being has been weakened through relying on machines, because the machines have been too complicated for him to manage; but in the future, though he will still be dehumanized, he will be dehumanized in a different way.
Thus the machine does weaken the capacity of the human mind.
